label: q fed back as input late in the copy phase
explanation: Fires almost only (>99.8% of mass) on copy-phase steps whose input is the token q, i.e. the model has just emitted q and it is fed back. It almost never fires on q in the original sequence or on any other input token. Position gates it strongly: the firing rate on copy-phase q inputs climbs with absolute step t (about 0 before t=8, 0.2% at t=10, 1.8% at t=13, about 3% at t>=14), so most mass sits in long sequences (L=8-9) at recall_idx >= 5. The largest activations are q inputs at t=16-17 (q at original position 7). Early copy-phase q inputs (t<13) give weak, partial activations, and these make up most of the misses. Some late q inputs stay silent, mainly at t=12-13 where q was at original position 3, so precision is incomplete. Output token, previous tokens and digit count have little effect.

issues: The core identification holds. Of the activation mass, 99.9% is in the copy phase, and in_tok==q carries 100% of it. Precision for q inputs in the original phase is 0.0006. Copy-phase q alone scores P 0.254 / R 0.996 on test, as claimed.

One stated fact is wrong. The explanation says the firing rate on copy-phase q inputs is about 0.2% at t=10, 1.8% at t=13 and about 3% at t>=14. Those are firing rates over all steps (the profile's by-t table), not rates conditional on a q input. The conditional rates are much higher. By (L, recall_idx) cell: t=13 is about 0.53-0.55; t=14 is 0.73 (L8) and 0.83 (L9); t=15 is 0.90-0.97; t=16-17 is about 0.94. Below t=12 the rate is 0.0-0.17.

Position is not purely absolute t. At t=12 the rate is 0.28 (L7, r5) and 0.32 (L8, r4) but only 0.04 (L9, r3). At t=11 it is 0.17 (L7) vs 0.003 (L9, r2). So a low recall_idx also suppresses firing. Even so, adding recall_idx terms did not raise F1: t>=13 | (t==12 & r>=4) gives 0.779 and t+recall_idx>=17 gives 0.786.

The claim that silent late q inputs come 'mainly at t=12-13 where q was at original position 3' is not specific. At t=13 the rate is about 0.53-0.55 whether q was at original position 3, 4 or 5. The silence comes from the ramp's midpoint, not from a particular position.

The claim that the output token has little effect is too strong. When the output is also q (a repeated q), the rate rises from 0.059 to 0.32 for t<=12 and from 0.77 to 0.985 for t>=13. Digit-heavy sequences also fire a bit more (0.85 with n_digits>=3 vs 0.72 with n_digits==0 at t>=13). These are small subsets.

The misses on the test split form one class: weak activations (about 0.01-0.25 of max) on copy-phase q inputs at t=9-12. That is 4086 steps holding 6.5% of the mass. The false positives are copy-phase q inputs at t=13-14 that stay silent, about 45% of the t=13 cell. Both come from thresholding a graded ramp in t, not from a missing token or history factor. I found no hidden determinant within the t=13 cell: in_count, correct, prev_tok class and to_go all sit at about 0.53-0.57.

Test F1 is 0.797, below the 0.8 bar, and the predicate is close to the ceiling for a binary rule on this ramp. The best variant I found, adding the repeated-q case, reaches only 0.801. The label itself is accurate, but the false conditional-rate figures and the overstated 'no output-token effect' mean the explanation as written does not fully check out.
skeptic.revised_label: q fed back as input in the copy phase, rising steeply with position (about 50% firing at t=13, over 90% at t>=15)
